senses.gloss: pr. n. pl.Harpania (Hipparenum, Neub. Géogr. p. 335; p. 352) in Babylonia, a rich industrial town with a Jewish population of spurious descent.
units: <cite ref="Yevamot 17a:7">Yeb. 17ᵃ</cite> what a great man, <he>אי לאו דה׳ מאתיה</he> were not H. his native town! <cite ref="Yevamot 17a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>מאי ה׳</he>, v. <cite ref="E00808"><he>הַר</he></cite>.
Sabb. 127ᵃ (Ms. M. הרדפנאי, read הַרְפְּנָאֵי Harpanians); B. Mets. 84ᵃ דה׳ Ms. M. (ed. דהַרְפְּנָאֵי) v. דְּקוּרָא.
Snh. 48ᵇ (Ms. M. נהר פניא) [Kidd. 72ᵇ Ms. O. הפרניא והימניא, ed. only הומניא.]—Denom. הַרְפְּנָאָה m. of H.
<cite ref="Eruvin 59b:10">Erub. 59ᵇ</cite> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 90).—Pl. <he>הַרְפְּנָאֵי</he>, v. supra.
